title: Changing the subject of a formula
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No existing point teaches rearranging a formula to change its subject; the closest points cover functions and solving equations, which are different ideas.

draft.title: Changing the subject of a formula
card: The subject of a formula is the letter on its own on one side. In v = d ÷ t, the subject is v.
To change the subject, do the same operation to both sides. Undo operations on the wanted letter in reverse order, so the last one applied is undone first.
Example: make d the subject of v = d ÷ t. Multiply both sides by t. This gives v × t = d, so d = vt.
Example: make x the subject of y = 3x + 2. Subtract 2 from both sides: y − 2 = 3x. Then divide both sides by 3: x = (y − 2) ÷ 3.
draft.remember: Do the same to both sides, and undo the steps in reverse order.

a.q: Make m the subject of P = 4m − 5
a.why: First add 5 to both sides: P + 5 = 4m. Then divide both sides by 4 to get m = (P + 5) ÷ 4. Option m = P ÷ 4 + 5 is tempting, but it divides only part of the right side, so the 5 is not divided by 4.
a.clue: Undo the subtraction first, then the multiplication.

b.q: The formula C = 5F ÷ 9 is rearranged to make F the subject. Which result is correct?
b.why: Multiply both sides by 9: 9C = 5F. Then divide both sides by 5: F = 9C ÷ 5. Option F = 5C ÷ 9 is tempting, but it swaps the numbers and does not undo the operations.
b.clue: Undo the division by 9 first, then undo the multiplication by 5.
